title: Websites Go Dark as AI Finds Critical PHP Flaws Affecting Most of the Internet
excerpt: Two flaws in PHP, found in August by Calif with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and independently by Google-owned Wiz, forced governments from France to Australia to pull sites offline on Wednesday while a patch rolled out.
body:
• Two critical flaws in PHP — the programming language Wiz estimates runs about 70% of the world's websites — were disclosed on Wednesday after being found with help from AI models, and government and company sites worldwide took themselves offline as a precaution.
  • The flaws, collectively called PHP2Shell, can let attackers execute code remotely and read server memory that may contain passwords, according to Wiz, OpenAI and security firm Calif.
  • Security firm Calif found the flaws in August using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol in an OpenAI-funded audit; Google-owned Wiz found them independently weeks later using Gemini 4 Argon, Wiz Atlas and GPT-5.6 Sol.
  • If you run a PHP site — WordPress, Drupal, Joomla or Magento included — the PHP Foundation's instruction is to update now; the US National Security Agency told organisations to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline.

Government agencies and companies around the world shut down websites on Wednesday after two critical flaws were disclosed in PHP, the programming language underneath a large share of the internet. The Hindu's report describes operators from European governments to Wikipedia taking services offline as a precaution, while CNN reported the bugs could affect 70% of the internet. The flaws had been reported privately and kept confidential while a fix was prepared; details leaked online on Tuesday, a day before the planned release, forcing the rush.

What Was Found, and How AI Found It

The vulnerabilities, collectively called PHP2Shell, could allow attackers to execute code and read memory that could contain sensitive information such as passwords, and to take over web servers without needing a password. Wiz estimated PHP runs about 70% of the world's websites and said the flaws rank "among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history." Reuters, via Devdiscourse, reported the flaws had lurked in PHP for more than a decade until AI uncovered them.

https://x.com/BrianRoemmele/status/2112908500460552274

Security firm Calif found the flaws in August using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model, as part of an OpenAI-funded audit of PHP's code. Wiz said it found them independently weeks later with help from Google's Gemini 4 Argon, its own Wiz Atlas tool and GPT-5.6 Sol. "With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work," Wiz researchers wrote. OpenAI called the flaws "one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory."

"If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now."

— The PHP Foundation

Who Went Dark, and Why

Only sites that run PHP on their own servers are exposed; large platforms built on other languages, or able to install the fix quickly, stayed online. In France, local government websites including one for the Paris police were made inaccessible at the request of the French National Cybersecurity Agency. In the Netherlands, the national digital identity service DigiD, the House of Representatives website and the national cybersecurity centre went offline, as did the Port of Rotterdam and hospital sites, according to Reuters. Finland's state IT provider took government public network services offline, and Australia's Signals Directorate said its cyber.gov.au site was affected. The Wikimedia Foundation warned of outages on Wikipedia and took supporting services offline until they could be patched.

The urgency is driven by a race: because the fix is now public and AI tools can reverse-engineer the bug with little effort, experts braced for a wave of intrusions. AI was powering a "race to exploit," said Costin Raiu, co-founder of cybersecurity firm TLP:Black. Censys data cited by Reuters said about 1.5 million of 2.6 million hosts were running a PHP version for which there is no fix.

What Site Owners Must Do

PHP sits underneath WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento, so the exposed population includes online stores, news outlets and government services run by small teams on shared hosting. "All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable," said Tiffany Farriss, interim chief executive of the Drupal Association. The NSA said the flaws "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database." For Indian technology teams maintaining client sites abroad, the action is the same as everywhere else: apply the PHP update released Wednesday, or take the vulnerable system offline until it can be patched.

A Turning Point for AI and Security

Volker Dusch, a security engineer at the PHP Foundation, told the Wall Street Journal this was the most serious problem PHP had faced in more than a decade, comparing it to Heartbleed in 2014. The disclosure comes amid a surge in AI-driven security findings, with the number of vulnerabilities found in 2026 on track to roughly double last year's record.
